title: Etale cohomology of the local scheme at a point as a colimit over Zariski neighbourhoods
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], $x\in X$, $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ the local ring and $g_x:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] the canonical morphism; for every open $U\ni x$ it factors uniquely as $g_x=j_U\circ g_{x,U}$ with $j_U:U\hookrightarrow X$ the open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. For an open $U\subseteq X$ write $H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ for the cohomology of $\mathcal F$ over the object $U\hookrightarrow X$ of $X_{\Et}$ ([def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (2)), the restriction $H^q(U,\mathcal F)\to H^q(W,\mathcal F)$ for $W\subseteq U$ being induced by the restriction maps of an injective resolution of $\mathcal F$. Then $H^q(U,\mathcal F)=H^q(U_{\Et},j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)$ canonically, and the maps $H^q(U,\mathcal F)=H^q(U_{\Et},j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{g_{x,U}^*}H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_{x,U}^{-1}j_U^{-1}\mathcal F)\cong H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_x^{-1}\mathcal F)$ (pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] followed by the canonical isomorphism $g_{x,U}^{-1}j_U^{-1}\cong g_x^{-1}$ of inverse images [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]; etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]) are compatible with the restrictions and induce, for every $q\ge0$, an isomorphism
$$\varinjlim_{U\ni x\ \text{open}}H^q(U,\mathcal F)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_x^{-1}\mathcal F),$$
the colimit being over the open neighbourhoods of $x$ ordered by reverse inclusion (a directed set). In particular a class $\xi\in H^q(U,\mathcal F)$ whose image in $H^q((\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})_{\Et},g_x^{-1}\mathcal F)$ is zero restricts to zero in $H^q(W,\mathcal F)$ for some open $x\in W\subseteq U$.

etale cohomology of Spec of local ring O_{X,x} is the colimit of etale cohomology of open neighbourhoods of x
